translations.idiomatic: When Shen was summoned from Dingzhou as director of the Ministry of Personnel with central guards, Shun drafted the edict, wording beautiful.

sentences.zh: 徽疑順為深左右，由是與徐紇間順于靈太后。

translations.literal: Hui suspected Shun was Shen's man at court; therefore with Xu Chi he slandered Shun to Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Hui suspected Shun was Shen's man; with Xu Chi he slandered Shun to the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 出順為護軍將軍、太常卿。

translations.literal: Shun was sent out as Grand General Who Protects the Army and Grand Master of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was sent out as Grand General Who Protects the Army and grand master of rites.

sentences.zh: 順奉辭於西遊園，徽、紇侍側。

translations.literal: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden; Hui and Chi attended at the side.
translations.idiomatic: Shun took leave in the Western Tour Garden; Hui and Chi attended.

sentences.zh: 順指謂靈太后曰：「此人魏之宰嚭，魏國不滅，終不死亡。

translations.literal: Shun pointed and told Empress Dowager Ling: "This man is Wei's Bo Pi—if Wei is not destroyed he will not die.
translations.idiomatic: Shun pointed and told her, "This man is Wei's Bo Pi—if Wei is not destroyed he will not die.

sentences.zh: 」紇協肩而出。

translations.literal: " He Ruo hunched his shoulders and walked out.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu He hunched his shoulders and walked out.

sentences.zh: 順因抗聲叱之曰：「一介刀筆小人，正堪為几案之吏，甯應忝茲執戟，虧我彝倫！

translations.literal: Shun then shouted at him: "A mere clerk with brush and knife—fit only for a desk officer. How dare he hold a halberd here and shame our kinship!"
translations.idiomatic: Shun shouted after him, "A brush-and-knife clerk, fit only for a desk—how dare he bear a halberd here and shame our kinship!"

sentences.zh: 」遂振衣而起。

translations.literal: " He flung his robe and rose.
translations.idiomatic: " He flung his robe aside and stood.

sentences.zh: 靈太后默而不言。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager said nothing.

sentences.zh: 時追論順父顧托之功，增任城王彝邑二千戶，又析彝邑五百以封順為東阿縣公。

translations.literal: At the time they were reviewing Shun's father's merit in the imperial entrustment; Prince of Rencheng Yi was given an additional fief of two thousand households, and five hundred of Yi's fief was split off to enfeoff Shun as Duke of Dong'a.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then reviewing Shun's father's merit in the imperial entrustment; Prince of Rencheng Yi received two thousand additional households, and five hundred of Yi's fief was carved out to make Shun Duke of Dong'a.

sentences.zh: 順疾徽等間之，遂為《蒼蠅賦》。

translations.literal: Shun, fearing that Hui and the others were undermining him, thereupon wrote "The Flies."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Hui and the others were undermining him, Shun wrote "The Flies."

sentences.zh: 屬疾在家，杜絕慶吊。

translations.literal: When illness kept him at home, he cut off all congratulations and condolences.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him at home; he refused all congratulations and condolences.

sentences.zh: 後除吏部尚書，兼右僕射，與城陽王徽同日拜職。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Right Vice Director, receiving office the same day as Prince of Chengyang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent right vice director, taking office the same day as Prince of Chengyang Hui.

sentences.zh: 舍人鄭儼於止車門外先謁徽，後拜順。

translations.literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Zheng Yan first paid court to Hui outside the Halting Carriage Gate, then bowed to Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Zheng Yan first paid court to Hui outside the Halting Carriage Gate, then bowed to Shun.

sentences.zh: 順怒曰：「卿是佞人，當拜佞王。

translations.literal: Shun said in anger: "You are a flatterer—you should bow to a flatterer's prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shun said in anger, "You are a flatterer—you should bow to a flatterer's prince.

sentences.zh: 我是直人，不受曲拜。

translations.literal: I am an upright man and do not accept a crooked bow."
translations.idiomatic: I am an upright man and will not accept a crooked bow."

sentences.zh: 」儼深懷謝。

translations.literal: Yan was deeply apologetic.
translations.idiomatic: Yan apologized deeply.

sentences.zh: 順曰：「卿是高門子弟，而為北宮幸臣，僕射李思沖尚與王洛誠同傳，以此度之，卿亦應繼其卷下。

translations.literal: Shun said: "You are a son of a great house, yet you are a favorite of the Northern Palace; Vice Director Li Sichong still shares a scroll with Wang Luocheng—by that measure you too should follow on the next roll."
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "You are a son of a great house, yet a favorite of the Northern Palace; Vice Director Li Sichong still shares a scroll with Wang Luocheng—by that measure you belong on the next roll too."

sentences.zh: 」見者為之震動，而順安然自得。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were shaken, while Shun remained perfectly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers were shaken; Shun remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 及上省，登階向榻，見榻甚故，問都令史徐仵起。

translations.literal: When he went up to the Secretariat and climbed the steps toward the couch, he saw the couch was very old and asked the chief clerical officer Xu Wuqi.
translations.idiomatic: Going up to the Secretariat and climbing toward the couch, he found it very old and asked the chief clerical officer Xu Wuqi.

sentences.zh: 仵起曰：「此榻曾經先王坐。

translations.literal: Wuqi said: "This couch once had the late emperor sit on it."
translations.idiomatic: Wuqi said, "The late emperor once sat on this couch."

sentences.zh: 」順即哽塞，涕泗交流，久而不能言，遂令換之。

translations.literal: Shun at once choked up; tears streamed down; for a long time he could not speak, and he ordered it replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Shun choked up; tears streamed; long he could not speak, and he ordered it replaced.

sentences.zh: 時三公曹令史硃暉素事錄尚書、高陽王雍，雍欲以為廷尉評，頻煩托順，順不為用。

translations.literal: At the time the chief clerical officer of the Three Offices Cao, Zhu Hui, had long served Recording Director Prince of Gaoyang Yong; Yong wished to make him a reviewer of the Court of Justice and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun would not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hui, chief clerical officer of the Three Offices Cao, had long served Recording Director Prince of Gaoyang Yong; Yong wished to make him a Court of Justice reviewer and repeatedly pressed Shun, but Shun refused.

sentences.zh: 雍遂下命用之，順投之於地。

translations.literal: Yong then issued an order to use him; Shun threw it to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yong issued an order appointing him; Shun threw it to the floor.

sentences.zh: 雍聞之，大怒，昧爽坐都査，召尚書及丞郎畢集，欲待順至，於眾挫之。

translations.literal: When Yong heard of it he was greatly angered; at dawn he sat in the metropolitan review hall, summoned the director and all the section chiefs to gather, intending to wait for Shun's arrival and humiliate him before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was furious; at dawn he sat in the metropolitan review hall and summoned the director and all section chiefs, intending to humble Shun before them when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 順日高方至。

translations.literal: Shun came only when the sun was high.
translations.idiomatic: Shun arrived only when the sun stood high.

sentences.zh: 雍攘袂撫幾而言曰：「身天子之子，天子之弟，天子之叔，天子之相，四海之內，親尊莫二。

translations.literal: Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said: "I am the Son of Heaven's son, the Son of Heaven's younger brother, the Son of Heaven's uncle, the Son of Heaven's chief minister—within the four seas none is more honored.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rolled up his sleeves, struck the table, and said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son, brother, uncle, and chief minister—within the four seas none stands higher.

sentences.zh: 元順何人，以身成命投棄於地！

translations.literal: What sort of man is Yuan Shun, that he throws my written order to the ground!"
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man is Yuan Shun, to throw my written order to the ground!"

sentences.zh: 」順須鬢俱張，仰面看屋，憤氣奔湧，長歔而不言。

translations.literal: Shun's beard bristled; he looked up at the rafters; rage surged; he sighed long and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's beard bristled; he looked up at the rafters; rage surged; he sighed long and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 久之，搖一白羽扇，徐而謂雍曰：「高祖遷宅中土，創定九流，官方清濁，軌儀萬古。

translations.literal: After a long while he waved a white feather fan and said slowly to Yong: "The High Ancestor moved the capital to the central lands and fixed the nine ranks; official grades were set clear and dark, a model for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he waved a white feather fan and said slowly to Yong, "The High Ancestor moved the capital to the central lands and fixed the nine ranks; grades were set clear and dark, a model for ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 而硃暉小人，身為省吏，何合為廷尉清官？

translations.literal: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, a clerical officer of the Secretariat—how is he fit to be a clean official of the Court of Justice?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhu Hui is a petty man, a Secretariat clerk—how is he fit for a clean post in the Court of Justice?

sentences.zh: 殿下既先皇同氣，誠宜遵旨，自有恆規，而復逾之也？

translations.literal: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood; you truly ought to follow the edict and keep to the constant rule—why overstep it again?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness shares the late emperor's blood; you ought to follow the edict and keep to the constant rule—why overstep it again?"

sentences.zh: 」雍曰：「身為丞相、錄尚書，如何不得用一人為官？

translations.literal: Yong said: "As chief minister and recording director, how may I not appoint one man to office?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "As chief minister and recording director, how may I not appoint one man to office?"

sentences.zh: 」順曰：「庖人雖不理庖，屍祝不越樽俎而代之。

translations.literal: Shun said: "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the corpse-blesser does not step past the wine-vessel and stand in for him.
translations.idiomatic: Shun said, "Though the cook does not manage the kitchen, the corpse-blesser does not step past the wine-vessel and stand in for him.

sentences.zh: 未聞有別旨令殿下參選事。

translations.literal: I have not heard of any separate edict ordering Your Highness to participate in selections."
translations.idiomatic: I have not heard of any separate edict ordering Your Highness to participate in selections."

sentences.zh: 」順又厲聲曰：「殿下必如是，順當依事奏聞。

translations.literal: Shun again said sharply: "If Your Highness insists, Shun will memorialize the matter to the throne."
translations.idiomatic: Shun said sharply again, "If Your Highness insists, Shun will memorialize the matter to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」雍遂笑而言曰：「豈可以硃暉小人，便相忿恨。

translations.literal: Yong then laughed and said: "How can one grow angry over a petty man like Zhu Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Yong laughed and said, "How can one grow angry over a petty man like Zhu Hui."

sentences.zh: 」遂起，呼順入室，與之極飲。

translations.literal: He rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He rose, called Shun into the inner room, and drank with him to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 順之亢毅不撓，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's lofty firmness and refusal to bend were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 後兼左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he was made Concurrent Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made concurrent left vice director.

sentences.zh: 氽硃榮之奉莊帝，召百官悉至河陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuangdi, he summoned all the hundred officials to Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong received Emperor Zhuangdi, he summoned all the hundred officials to Heyin.

sentences.zh: 素聞順數諫諍，惜其亮直，謂硃瑞曰：「可語元僕射，但在省，不須來。

translations.literal: He had long heard that Shun often remonstrated; he prized his bright integrity and told Zhu Rui: "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay at the Secretariat—he need not come."
translations.idiomatic: He had long heard Shun often remonstrated; he prized his bright integrity and told Zhu Rui, "Tell Vice Director Yuan to stay at the Secretariat—he need not come."

sentences.zh: 」順不達其旨，聞害衣冠，遂便出走，為陵戶鮮于康奴所害。

translations.literal: Shun did not grasp his meaning; hearing that the officials were to be harmed, he fled at once and was killed by tomb-guard Xianyu Kangnu.
translations.idiomatic: Shun did not grasp his meaning; hearing that the officials were to be harmed, he fled and was killed by tomb-guard Xianyu Kangnu.

sentences.zh: 家徒四壁，無物僉槠，止有書數千卷而已。

translations.literal: His house had bare walls and no goods to store—only several thousand volumes of books.
translations.idiomatic: His house had bare walls and nothing to store—only several thousand volumes of books.

sentences.zh: 門下通事令史王才達裂裳覆之。

translations.literal: Gentleman-in-Attendance Wang Caida tore his robe to cover him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-in-Attendance Wang Caida tore his robe to cover him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，遣黃門侍郎山偉巡喻京邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour and announce the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi returned to the palace, he sent Yellow Gate Attendant Shan Wei to tour the capital and announce the restoration.

sentences.zh: 偉臨順喪，悲慟無已。

translations.literal: Wei came to Shun's mourning hall and wept without end.
translations.idiomatic: Wei came to Shun's mourning hall and wept without end.

sentences.zh: 既還，莊帝怪其聲散，偉以狀對。

translations.literal: When he returned, Emperor Zhuangdi wondered at his broken voice; Wei reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the emperor wondered at his broken voice; Wei reported what he had seen.

sentences.zh: 莊帝敕侍中元祉曰：「宗室喪亡非一，不可周贍。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangdi ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Zhi: "The imperial clan has not suffered one death alone—it cannot all be compensated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Zhi, "The imperial clan has lost more than one man—it cannot all be compensated.

sentences.zh: 元僕射清苦之節，死乃益彰，特贈絹百匹，餘不得為例。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yuan's integrity in poverty shines brighter in death; grant him a special gift of a hundred bolts of silk—let no other case follow this."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan's integrity in poverty shines brighter in death; grant a special gift of a hundred bolts of silk—let no other case follow."

sentences.zh: 」贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰文烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在籓，順夢一段黑雲從西北直來，觸東南上日月俱破，復翳諸星，天地盡暗。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was still in his princedom, Shun dreamed that a stretch of black cloud came straight from the northwest, struck the sun and moon in the southeast and broke them both, then veiled all the stars; heaven and earth were wholly dark.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the emperor was still in his princedom, Shun dreamed a stretch of black cloud came straight from the northwest, struck the sun and moon in the southeast and broke them, veiled all the stars, and left heaven and earth wholly dark.

sentences.zh: 俄而雲消霧散，便有日出自西南隅，甚明淨，雲長樂王日。

translations.literal: Soon the cloud and mist dispersed, and the sun came out from the southwest corner, very bright and clear; the cloud was long, the Prince of Changle's sun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon cloud and mist dispersed; the sun came out from the southwest corner, bright and clear—the cloud was long, the Prince of Changle's sun.

sentences.zh: 尋見莊帝從閶闔門入，登太極殿，唱萬歲者三，百官咸加朝服謁帝，唯順集書省步廊西槐樹下，脫衣冠臥。

translations.literal: Presently he saw Emperor Zhuangdi enter from the Changhe Gate, ascend the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and three times the cry of "ten thousand years" went up; the hundred officials all put on court dress to attend the emperor, while Shun alone, in the western corridor of the Secretariat by the locust tree, removed cap and robe and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he saw Emperor Zhuangdi enter from Changhe Gate, ascend the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and "ten thousand years" ring out three times; officials all donned court dress to attend, while Shun alone in the Secretariat's western corridor by the locust tree removed cap and robe and lay down.

sentences.zh: 既寤，告元暉業曰：「吾昨夜夢，於我殊自不佳。

translations.literal: When he woke he told Yuan Huiye: "My dream last night was very bad for me."
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he told Yuan Huiye, "My dream last night was very bad for me."

sentences.zh: 」說夢，因解之曰：「黑雲，氣之惡者，是北方之色，終當必有北敵，以亂京師，害二宮，殘毀百僚。

translations.literal: He told the dream and interpreted it: "Black cloud is the color of ill qi, the color of the north—there will surely be a northern enemy who will disorder the capital, harm the two palaces, and ruin the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: He told the dream and interpreted it: "Black cloud is ill qi, the color of the north—a northern enemy will surely disorder the capital, harm the two palaces, and ruin the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 日，君象也。

translations.literal: The sun is the image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The sun is the image of the ruler.

sentences.zh: 月，後象也。

translations.literal: The moon is the image of the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The moon is the image of the empress.

sentences.zh: 眾星，百官象也。

translations.literal: The host of stars are the image of the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: The host of stars are the image of the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，京邑其當禍乎？

translations.literal: By this reasoning, will not the capital suffer calamity?
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, will not the capital suffer calamity?

sentences.zh: 昔劉曜破晉室以為髑髏台，前途之事，得無此乎？

translations.literal: Formerly Liu Yao destroyed the Jin house and made a platform of skulls—will not what lies ahead be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Liu Yao destroyed the Jin house and made a platform of skulls—will not what lies ahead be like this?

sentences.zh: 雖然，彭城王勰有文德於天下，今夢其兒為天子，積德必報，此必然矣！

translations.literal: Even so, Prince of Pengcheng Xie had civil virtue throughout the realm; now the dream shows his son as Son of Heaven—accumulated virtue must be rewarded; this is certain!
translations.idiomatic: Even so, Prince of Pengcheng Xie had civil virtue throughout the realm; now the dream shows his son as Son of Heaven—accumulated virtue must be rewarded; this is certain.

sentences.zh: 但恨其得之不久。

translations.literal: I only regret that he will not hold it long.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret he will not hold it long.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，出自西南，以時易年，不過三載。

translations.literal: The reason is that he comes from the southwest; by the season changing the year, it will not exceed three years.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is he comes from the southwest; by season changing year, it will not exceed three years.

sentences.zh: 但恨我不見之。

translations.literal: I only regret that I will not see it.
translations.idiomatic: I only regret I will not see it.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 我夢臥槐樹下，槐字木傍鬼，身與鬼並，復解冠冕，此寧不死乎！

translations.literal: I dreamed I lay under a locust tree; the character for locust has 'tree' beside 'ghost'—my person and a ghost together; again I removed cap and robe—will this not mean death?
translations.idiomatic: I dreamed I lay under a locust tree; locust has 'tree' beside 'ghost'—my person and a ghost together; again I removed cap and robe—will this not mean death?

sentences.zh: 然亡後乃得三公贈耳。

translations.literal: Yet after death I shall receive the three dukes' posthumous gift."
translations.idiomatic: Yet after death I shall receive the three dukes' posthumous gift."

sentences.zh: 」皆如其夢。

translations.literal: All came about as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: All came about as in the dream.

sentences.zh: 順撰《帝錄》二十卷，詩賦表頌數十篇，並多亡失。

translations.literal: Shun compiled "Records of Emperors" in twenty scrolls, and several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies—most are now lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shun compiled Records of Emperors in twenty scrolls and several tens of poems, rhapsodies, memorials, and eulogies—most are now lost.

sentences.zh: 長子朗，時年十七，枕戈潛伏積年，乃手刃康奴，以首祭順墓，然後詣闕請罪。

translations.literal: His eldest son Lang, then seventeen, lay with a blade in hiding for many years, then with his own hand cut down Kangnu and offered the head at Shun's tomb, then went to the palace gate to confess his crime.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Lang, then seventeen, lay with a blade in hiding for years, then with his own hand cut down Kangnu and offered the head at Shun's tomb, then went to the palace gate to confess.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉而不問。

translations.literal: The court praised him and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 朗位司徒屬。

translations.literal: Lang held the office of Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lang held the office of Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為奴所害，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was killed by a slave; posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he was killed by a slave and was posthumously made right vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 順弟紀，字子綱，隨孝武入關中，位尚書左僕射、華山郡王。

translations.literal: Shun's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Zigang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and held Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Huashan.
translations.idiomatic: Shun's younger brother Ji, courtesy name Zigang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and held left vice director of the Masters of Writing and the title Prince of Huashan.

sentences.zh: 南安王楨，皇興二年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Nan'an Zhen was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，累遷長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he rose to Grand General of the Chang'an Garrison and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 楨性忠謹。

translations.literal: Zhen by nature was loyal and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was loyal and careful by nature.

sentences.zh: 其母疾篤，憂毀異常，遂有白雉遊其庭前。

translations.literal: When his mother's illness was grave, his grief and emaciation were extraordinary; then a white pheasant wandered before his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother's illness grew grave, his grief and emaciation were extraordinary; then a white pheasant wandered in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其致感，賜帛千匹以褒美之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of his moving heaven and earth and gave a thousand bolts of silk to praise and honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard how he had moved heaven and earth and gave a thousand bolts of silk in praise.

sentences.zh: 征赴講武，引見於皇信堂，戒之曰：「公孝行著於私庭，令問彰于邦國，既國之懿親，終無貧賤之慮。

translations.literal: Summoned to lecture on military affairs and received audience in the Hall of Imperial Trust, he was admonished: "Your filial conduct shows in your private hall and your fair name shines in the realm; as a close kin of the state you will never know poverty or low station.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to lecture on military affairs and received in the Hall of Imperial Trust, he was admonished: "Your filial conduct shows at home and your fair name in the realm; as close kin of the state you will never know poverty.

sentences.zh: 所宜慎者略有三事：一者恃親驕矜，違禮僭度；

translations.literal: What you should beware of is roughly three things: first, relying on kinship and acting arrogant, violating ritual and overstepping measure;
translations.idiomatic: What you should beware of is roughly three things: first, relying on kinship, acting arrogant, violating ritual and overstepping measure;

sentences.zh: 二者傲慢貪奢，不恤政事；

translations.literal: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury, not caring for government;
translations.idiomatic: second, arrogance, greed, and luxury, not caring for government;

sentences.zh: 三者飲酒遊逸，不擇交友。

translations.literal: third, drinking wine, roaming in pleasure, and not choosing whom you befriend.
translations.idiomatic: third, drinking, roaming in pleasure, and not choosing whom you befriend.

sentences.zh: 三者不去，患禍將生。

translations.literal: If you do not cast off these three, disaster and calamity will be born."
translations.idiomatic: Cast off none of these three and disaster will be born."

sentences.zh: 」而楨不能遵奉，後乃聚斂肆情。

translations.literal: Zhen could not follow and obey; afterward he gathered wealth and indulged his desires.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen could not follow and obey; afterward he gathered wealth and indulged his desires.

sentences.zh: 孝文以楨孝養聞名內外，特加原恕，削除封爵，以庶人歸第，禁錮終身。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Zhen's filial nurture was famed within and without, especially pardoned him, stripped his enfeoffment, sent him home as a commoner, and confined him for life.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen, because Zhen's filial nurture was famed within and without, especially pardoned him, stripped his enfeoffment, sent him home as a commoner, and confined him for life.

sentences.zh: 以議定遷都，復封南安王，為鎮北大將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Because he took part in deciding the move of the capital, he was again enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an, made Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because he took part in deciding the move of the capital, he was again enfeoffed Prince of Nan'an, made Grand General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 帝餞楨于華林都亭，詔並賦詩。

translations.literal: The emperor saw Zhen off at the Hualin Metropolitan Pavilion and ordered all to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw Zhen off at the Hualin Metropolitan Pavilion and ordered all to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 不能者，並可聽射，當使武士彎弓，文人下筆。

translations.literal: Those who could not might still be allowed to shoot arrows—warriors would bend the bow, men of letters take up the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could not might still shoot arrows—warriors would bend the bow, men of letters take up the brush.

sentences.zh: 帝送楨下階，流涕而別。

translations.literal: The emperor escorted Zhen down the steps, parting with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor escorted Zhen down the steps, parting in tears.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年五月，至鄴。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taihe he reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the twentieth year of Taihe he reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 上日，暴雨大風，凍死者數十人。

translations.literal: On the day of the imperial birthday, violent wind and rain struck; several tens froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the imperial birthday, violent wind and rain struck; several tens froze to death.

sentences.zh: 楨又以旱，祈雨於群神。

translations.literal: Zhen again, because of drought, prayed for rain to the host of spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again, because of drought, prayed for rain to the host of spirits.

sentences.zh: 鄴城有石季龍廟，人奉祀之。

translations.literal: In Ye city was the temple of Shi Jilong; the people worshipped it.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye stood the temple of Shi Jilong; the people worshipped it.

sentences.zh: 楨告神像云：「三日不雨，當加鞭罰。

translations.literal: Zhen told the spirit-image: "If in three days there is no rain, I will add the whip's punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told the spirit-image, "If in three days there is no rain, I will add the whip's punishment."

sentences.zh: 」請雨不驗，遂鞭像一百。

translations.literal: The prayer for rain did not succeed; he then whipped the image a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer for rain failed; he whipped the image a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 是月，疽發背薨，諡曰惠。

translations.literal: That month a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died; his posthumous title was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: That month a carbuncle broke on his back and he died; posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 及恆州刺史穆泰謀反，楨知而不告。

translations.literal: When Governor of Heng Province Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor of Heng Mu Tai plotted rebellion, Zhen knew and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 雖薨，猶追奪爵封，國除。

translations.literal: Though dead, his rank and fief were still stripped posthumously and the state abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Though dead, his rank and fief were still stripped posthumously and the state abolished.

sentences.zh: 子英，性識聰敏，善騎射，解音律，微曉醫術。

translations.literal: His son Ying by nature was clever and keen, skilled at riding and shooting, understood music, and knew a little medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying was clever and keen by nature, skilled at riding and shooting, understood music, and knew a little medicine.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，為梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 帝南伐，為漢中別道都將。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south he was Separate Route Commander-in-Chief of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south he was separate-route commander-in-chief of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 後大駕臨鐘離，英以大駕親動，勢傾東南，漢中有可乘之會，表求追討，帝許之。

translations.literal: Later, when the great host reached Zhongli, Ying because the imperial carriage moved in person and momentum tilted toward the southeast, and Hanzhong had an opening to exploit, memorialized asking to pursue and strike; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the great host reached Zhongli, Ying—seeing the emperor move in person, momentum tilt southeast, and Hanzhong open to exploit—memorialized asking to pursue and strike; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 以功遷安南大將軍，賜爵廣武伯。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed Earl of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted to Grand General Who Pacifies the South and enfeoffed Earl of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 既而梁入寇肥梁，詔英率眾十萬討之，所在皆以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Liang invaded Feiliang; an edict ordered Ying to lead a host of a hundred thousand to attack; wherever he went he was to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Liang invaded Feiliang; an edict ordered Ying to lead a hundred thousand men to attack; wherever he went he was to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 英表陳事機，乃擊破陰陵，斬梁將二十五人，及虜首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized the timing of events and thereupon broke Yinling, beheading twenty-five Liang generals and more than five thousand heads of captives.
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized the timing of events, broke Yinling, beheaded twenty-five Liang generals, and took more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又頻破梁軍于梁城，斬其支將四十二人，殺獲及溺死者將五萬。

translations.literal: He again repeatedly defeated Liang armies at Liangcheng, beheading forty-two of their detached generals; killed, captured, and drowned came to nearly fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He again repeatedly defeated Liang armies at Liangcheng, beheading forty-two detached generals; killed, captured, and drowned came to nearly fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 梁中軍大將軍臨川王蕭宏、尚書左僕射柳惔等大將五人沿淮東走。

translations.literal: Liang Central Army Grand General Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Liu Yan, and five other great generals fled east along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Liang central-army grand general Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, left vice director Liu Yan, and five other great generals fled east along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 凡收米四十萬石。

translations.literal: In all they took forty myriads of grain.
translations.idiomatic: In all they took four hundred thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 英追奔至馬頭，梁馬頭戍主委城遁走，遂圍鐘離。

translations.literal: Ying pursued to Matou; the Matou garrison commandant of Liang entrusted the city and fled; he then besieged Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: Ying pursued to Matou; the Matou garrison commandant entrusted the city and fled; he then besieged Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 詔以師行已久，命英為振旅之意。

translations.literal: An edict said the army had been out long and ordered Ying to have the mind of shaking the troops loose.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said the army had been out long and ordered Ying to withdraw the host.

sentences.zh: 英表：「期至二月將末，三月之初，理在必克。

translations.literal: Ying memorialized: "The term runs to the end of the second month and the beginning of the third; victory is sure by principle.
translations.idiomatic: Ying memorialized, "The term runs to late second month and early third month; victory is sure by principle.

sentences.zh: 但自此月一日已來，霖雨連並，可謂天違人願。

translations.literal: But from the first of this month rain has joined day after day—one may say heaven goes against men's wish.
translations.idiomatic: But from the first of this month rain has joined day after day—heaven goes against men's wish.

sentences.zh: 然王者行師，舉動不易，不可以少致暌淹，便生異議。

translations.literal: Yet when the king's army moves, its action is not easy to change; one must not, because of a little delay, raise dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the king's army moves, its action is not easy to change; one must not, for a little delay, raise dissent.

sentences.zh: 願聞朝廷，特開遠略，少復賜寬，假以日月，無使為山之功，中途而廢。

translations.literal: I wish the court would especially open a far-reaching plan, grant a little more breadth, lend days and months, and not let the work of moving a mountain stop halfway."
translations.idiomatic: I wish the court would open a far-reaching plan, grant a little breadth, lend days and months, and not let the work of moving a mountain stop halfway."

sentences.zh: 」及四月，水盛破橋，英及諸將狼狽奔退，士眾沒者十有五六。

translations.literal: By the fourth month the water swelled and broke the bridge; Ying and the generals fled in disorder; of soldiers drowned, one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month the water swelled and broke the bridge; Ying and the generals fled in disorder; one or two soldiers in ten drowned.

sentences.zh: 英至揚州，遣使送節及衣冠、貂蟬、章綬，詔以付典。

translations.literal: Ying reached Yang Province, sent an envoy to deliver his tally and seals of office, sable tail, cicada insignia, and ribbon of rank; an edict ordered them handed to the keeper of regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Ying reached Yang Province and sent an envoy to deliver his tally, seals, sable tail, cicada insignia, and ribbon of rank; an edict ordered them handed to the keeper of regalia.

sentences.zh: 有司奏英經算失圖，案劾處死。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Ying's calculations failed in plan and impeached him for death.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized that Ying's calculations failed and impeached him for death.

sentences.zh: 詔恕死為百姓。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him to death and made him a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him from death and made him a commoner.

sentences.zh: 後京兆王愉反，復英王封，除使持節、假征東將軍、都督冀州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Ying's princely enfeoffment was restored; he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, acting Eastern Campaign General, and Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Ying's princely enfeoffment was restored; he was made bearer of the staff of authority, acting eastern campaign general, and commander-in-chief of Ji military affairs.

sentences.zh: 英未發而冀州已平。

translations.literal: Before Ying set out, Ji Province was already pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before Ying set out, Ji was already pacified.

sentences.zh: 時郢州中從事督榮祖潛引梁軍，以義陽應之，三關之戍並據城降梁。

translations.literal: At the time the middle attendant of Ying Province, Supervisor Rongzu, secretly led Liang troops; they responded from Yiyang; garrisons of the Three Passes all held their cities and surrendered to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ying middle attendant Supervisor Rongzu secretly led Liang troops; Yiyang responded; garrisons of the Three Passes all held their cities and surrendered to Liang.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史婁悅嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Governor of Ying Lou Yue shut the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Ying Lou Yue shut the city and held it.

sentences.zh: 縣瓠人白早生等殺豫州刺史司馬悅，據城南叛。

translations.literal: Men of Xianbi, Bai Zaosheng and others, killed Governor of Yu Sima Yue and held the south of the city in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Xianbi, Bai Zaosheng and others, killed Governor of Yu Sima Yue and held the south of the city in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 梁將齊苟兒率眾守縣瓠。

translations.literal: Liang General Qi Gou'er led a host to hold Xianbi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Qi Gou'er led a host to hold Xianbi.

sentences.zh: 悅子尚華陽公主，並為所劫。

translations.literal: Yue's son Shang had married Princess Huayang; both were seized as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's son Shang had married Princess Huayang; both were seized as hostages.

sentences.zh: 詔英使持節、都督南征諸軍事、假征南將軍，出自汝南。

translations.literal: An edict made Ying Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of all Southern Campaign military affairs, and acting Southern Campaign General; he set out from Runan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Ying bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of southern campaign military affairs, and acting southern campaign general; he set out from Runan.

sentences.zh: 帝以刑巒頻破早生，詔英南赴義陽。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xing Luan had repeatedly defeated Zaosheng, ordered Ying south to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because Xing Luan had repeatedly defeated Zaosheng, ordered Ying south to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 英以眾少，累表請軍，帝不許。

translations.literal: Ying because his troops were few repeatedly memorialized asking for reinforcements; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, his troops being few, repeatedly memorialized for reinforcements; the emperor did not permit.

sentences.zh: 而英輒與邢巒分兵共攻縣瓠，ＩＮ之，乃引軍而南。

translations.literal: Yet Ying on his own authority joined Xing Luan in dividing troops to attack Xianbi together, captured it, then led the army south.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Ying on his own authority joined Xing Luan in dividing troops to attack Xianbi, captured it, then led the army south.

sentences.zh: 既次義陽，將取三關。

translations.literal: Having halted at Yiyang, he was about to take the Three Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Having halted at Yiyang, he was about to take the Three Passes.

sentences.zh: 英策之曰：「三關相須如左右手，若ＩＮ一關，而二關不待攻而定。

translations.literal: Ying calculated: "The three passes depend on one another like left and right hands; if one pass is taken, the other two need not wait for attack to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Ying calculated, "The three passes depend on one another like left and right hands; capture one pass and the other two need not wait for attack to be settled.

sentences.zh: 攻難不如易，東關易攻，宜須先取，即黃石公所謂戰如風發，攻如河決也。

translations.literal: Hard attack is not as good as easy; the eastern pass is easy to attack—you should first take it, as Huang Shigong said: battle like wind rising, attack like a river breaking its banks."
translations.idiomatic: Hard attack is not as good as easy; the eastern pass is easy—you should first take it, as Huang Shigong said: battle like wind rising, attack like a river breaking its banks."

sentences.zh: 」英恐其並力於東，乃使長史李華率五統向西關，分其兵勢，身督諸軍向東關。

translations.literal: Ying feared they would combine strength in the east; he therefore sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five detachments toward the western pass to divide their military momentum, while he himself directed the host toward the eastern pass.
translations.idiomatic: Ying feared they would combine in the east; he sent Chief Clerk Li Hua with five detachments toward the western pass to divide their strength, while he directed the host toward the eastern pass.

sentences.zh: 果如英策。

translations.literal: It was indeed as Ying had calculated.
translations.idiomatic: It was indeed as Ying had calculated.

sentences.zh: 凡禽其大將六人、支將二十人、卒七千、米四十萬石，軍資稱是。

translations.literal: In all they captured six great generals, twenty detached generals, seven thousand soldiers, forty myriads of grain, and military stores in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: In all they captured six great generals, twenty detached generals, seven thousand soldiers, four hundred thousand piculs of grain, and military stores in full measure.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On return to court he was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On return to court he was made vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司徒公，諡獻武王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously made duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 英子熙，字真興，好學俊爽，有文才，聲著於世。

translations.literal: Ying's son Xi, courtesy name Zhenxing, loved learning and was handsome and bright, had literary talent, and his fame resounded in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's son Xi, courtesy name Zhenxing, loved learning, was handsome and bright, had literary talent, and his fame resounded in the age.

sentences.zh: 然輕躁浮動，英深慮非保家之主，常欲廢之，立第四子略。

translations.literal: Yet he was frivolous and restless; Ying deeply feared he was not a man to preserve the house and often wished to depose him and establish the fourth son Lue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was frivolous and restless; Ying deeply feared he was not a man to preserve the house and often wished to depose him and establish the fourth son Lue.

sentences.zh: 略固請乃止。

translations.literal: Lue firmly begged and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Lue firmly begged and only then did he stop.

sentences.zh: 累遷光祿勳。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 時領軍於忠執政。

translations.literal: At the time the commander of the guards Yu Zhong held power.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong held power.

sentences.zh: 熙，忠之婿也，故歲中驟遷。

translations.literal: Xi was Zhong's son-in-law; therefore within the year he was suddenly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Zhong's son-in-law; therefore within the year he was suddenly promoted.

sentences.zh: 後授相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Xiang.

sentences.zh: 熙以七月上，其日大風寒雨，凍死者二十餘人，驢馬數十匹。

translations.literal: Xi took office in the seventh month; that day great wind and cold rain struck; more than twenty froze to death, and several tens of donkeys and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Xi took office in the seventh month; that day great wind and cold rain struck; more than twenty froze to death, and several tens of donkeys and horses.

sentences.zh: 熙聞其祖父前事，心惡之。

translations.literal: Xi heard of his grandfather's earlier affair and hated it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Xi heard of his grandfather's earlier affair and hated it in his heart.

sentences.zh: 又有蛆生其庭。

translations.literal: Again maggots were born in his courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Again maggots were born in his courtyard.

sentences.zh: 初，熙兄弟並為清河王懌所昵，及劉騰、元叉隔絕二宮，矯詔殺懌，熙乃起兵討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi and his brothers had all been favored by Prince of Qinghe Yi; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha cut off the two palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi thereupon raised troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xi and his brothers had all been favored by Prince of Qinghe Yi; when Liu Teng and Yuan Cha cut off the two palaces and forged an edict to kill Yi, Xi raised troops to punish them.

sentences.zh: 熙起兵甫十日，為其長史柳元章、別駕游荊、魏郡太守李孝怡執熙置之高樓，並其子弟。

translations.literal: Ten days after Xi raised troops, his chief clerk Liu Yuanzhang, vice director You Jing, and Administrator of Wei Commandery Li Xiaoyi seized Xi and placed him in a high tower, together with his sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after Xi raised troops, his chief clerk Liu Yuanzhang, vice director You Jing, and Wei commandery administrator Li Xiaoyi seized Xi and placed him in a high tower, together with his sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 叉遣尚書左丞盧同斬之於鄴街，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Cha sent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Tong to behead him in the streets of Ye and send the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cha sent left assistant director Lu Tong to behead him in the streets of Ye and send the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 始熙妃於氏知熙必敗，不從其謀，自初哭泣不絕，至於熙死。

translations.literal: At first Xi's consort, Lady Yu, knowing Xi would surely fail, did not follow his plans; from the first she wept without cease, until Xi's death.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xi's consort Lady Yu, knowing he would surely fail, did not follow his plans; from the first she wept without cease until his death.

sentences.zh: 熙既籓王，加有文學，風氣甚高。

translations.literal: Xi was a frontier prince and moreover had literary learning; his air was very high.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a frontier prince and moreover had literary learning; his bearing was very high.

sentences.zh: 始鎮鄴，知友才學之士袁翻、李琰之、李神俊、王誦兄弟、裴敬憲等咸餞于河梁，賦詩告別。

translations.literal: When he first took Ye as his garrison, learned friends and men of talent—Yuan Fan, Li Yanzhi, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others—all saw him off at the River Bridge and composed poems in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When he first garrisoned Ye, learned friends Yuan Fan, Li Yanzhi, Li Shenjun, the Wang Song brothers, Pei Jingxian, and others all saw him off at the River Bridge and composed farewell poems.

sentences.zh: 及將死，復與知故書，恨志意不遂。

translations.literal: When he was about to die he again wrote to old acquaintances, regretting that his will was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to die he again wrote to old acquaintances, regretting that his will was not fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 時人矜之。

translations.literal: Men of the time prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time prized him.

sentences.zh: 又，熙于任城王澄薨前，夢有人告之曰：「任城當死，死後二百日外，君亦不免。

translations.literal: Also, before Prince of Rencheng Cheng died, Xi dreamed someone told him: "Rencheng is about to die; two hundred days after his death you too will not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Also, before Prince of Rencheng Cheng died, Xi dreamed someone told him, "Rencheng is about to die; two hundred days after his death you too will not escape.

sentences.zh: 若其不信，試看任城家。

translations.literal: If you do not believe it, try looking at Rencheng's house."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not believe it, try looking at Rencheng's house."

sentences.zh: 」熙夢中顧瞻任城第舍，四面牆崩，無遺堵焉。

translations.literal: In the dream Xi looked back at Rencheng's residence; the walls on four sides collapsed; not one piece of wall remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the dream Xi looked back at Rencheng's residence; walls on four sides collapsed; not one piece remained.

sentences.zh: 熙惡之，覺而以告所親。

translations.literal: Xi hated it; waking, he told those close to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi hated it; waking, he told those close to him.

sentences.zh: 及熙之死也，果如所夢。

translations.literal: When Xi died it was indeed as in the dream.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi died it was indeed as in the dream.

sentences.zh: 熙兄弟三人，每從英征伐，在軍貪暴，或因迎降逐北，至有斬殺無辜，多增首級，以為功狀。

translations.literal: Xi's three brothers each followed Ying on campaign; in the army they were greedy and violent; sometimes in welcoming surrender and pursuing the routed they would cut down the innocent and add many heads to the merit rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's three brothers each followed Ying on campaign; in the army they were greedy and violent; sometimes in welcoming surrender and pursuing the routed they cut down the innocent and inflated head counts on the merit rolls.

sentences.zh: 又于忠誣郭祚、裴植也，忠意未決害之，由熙勸獎，遂至極法，世以為冤。

translations.literal: Again, when Yu Zhong slandered Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Zhong's mind had not yet settled on killing them; because Xi urged and encouraged him, they reached the extreme penalty—men of the age considered it a wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: Again, when Yu Zhong slandered Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi, Zhong's mind had not yet settled on killing them; Xi urged and encouraged him until they reached the extreme penalty—men of the age considered it wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 及熙之禍，識者以為有報應焉。

translations.literal: When Xi's calamity came, those who understood thought there was retribution.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi's calamity came, those who understood thought there was retribution.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，贈太尉公，諡曰文莊王。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager restored the government, he was posthumously made Grand Duke of the Secretariat; his posthumous title was Prince Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress Dowager restored the government, he was posthumously made grand duke of the Secretariat, posthumous title Prince Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 熙弟略，字亻雋興，位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Lue, courtesy name Juanxing, held the office of Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Lue, courtesy name Juanxing, held the office of gentleman attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 熙敗，略潛行，自托舊識河內司馬始賓。

translations.literal: When Xi failed, Lue fled in secret and entrusted himself to an old acquaintance, Interior Minister of Henei Sima Shibin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi failed, Lue fled in secret and entrusted himself to an old acquaintance, interior minister of Henei Sima Shibin.

sentences.zh: 始賓便為荻筏，夜與略俱渡盟津，詣上黨屯留縣栗法光家。

translations.literal: Shibin made a reed raft; at night he and Lue crossed the Meng Ford together and went to the house of Li Faguang of Tunliu in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Shibin made a reed raft; at night he and Lue crossed the Meng Ford and went to Li Faguang's house in Tunliu, Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 法光素敦信義，忻而納之。

translations.literal: Faguang by nature honored faith and righteousness; he rejoiced and received him.
translations.idiomatic: Faguang honored faith and righteousness by nature; he rejoiced and received him.

sentences.zh: 略舊識刁雙，時為西河太守，略復歸之。

translations.literal: Lue's old acquaintance Diao Shuang was then Governor of Xihe; Lue again went to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lue's old acquaintance Diao Shuang was then governor of Xihe; Lue went to him again.

sentences.zh: 停止經年，雙乃令從子昌送略潛遁江左。

translations.literal: He stayed more than a year; Shuang then had his nephew Chang escort Lue to slip away to the south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed more than a year; Shuang then had his nephew Chang escort Lue to slip away south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 梁武甚禮敬之，封中山王，宣城太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with great courtesy and respect, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made him Governor of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him with great courtesy, enfeoffed him Prince of Zhongshan, and made him governor of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而徐州刺史元法僧據城南叛，梁乃以略為大都督，令詣彭城接誘初附。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng held the south of the city in rebellion; Liang then made Lue Grand Commander-in-Chief and ordered him to Pengcheng to receive and entice the newly submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Faseng held the south of the city in rebellion; Liang made Lue grand commander-in-chief and ordered him to Pengcheng to receive the newly submitting.

sentences.zh: 尋征略與法僧同還。

translations.literal: Presently Lue was summoned back together with Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Lue was summoned back together with Faseng.

sentences.zh: 略雖在江南，自以家禍，晨夜哭泣，身若居喪。

translations.literal: Though Lue was in Jiangnan, because of his family's calamity he wept morning and night; his person was as if in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Though Lue was in Jiangnan, because of his family's calamity he wept morning and night; his person was as if in mourning.

sentences.zh: 又惡法僧為人，與法僧言，未嘗一笑。

translations.literal: He also hated Faseng's person; speaking with Faseng he never once smiled.
translations.idiomatic: He also hated Faseng's person; speaking with Faseng he never once smiled.

sentences.zh: 梁復除略衡州刺史，未行。

translations.literal: Liang again made Lue Governor of Heng Province; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Liang again made him governor of Heng; he did not go.

sentences.zh: 會其豫章王綜以城歸國，綜長史江革、司馬祖暼恆、將士五千人，悉見禽虜。

translations.literal: It happened that his Prince of Yuzhang Zong returned to the state with the city; Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, Marshal Zu Huanheng, and five thousand soldiers were all taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that his Prince of Yuzhang Zong returned to the state with the city; Zong's chief clerk Jiang Ge, marshal Zu Huanheng, and five thousand soldiers were all taken captive.

sentences.zh: 明帝敕有司悉遣革等還南，因以征略，梁乃備禮遣之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming ordered the relevant offices to send Ge and the rest back south; thereby they summoned Lue, and Liang then sent him off with full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered the relevant offices to send Ge and the rest back south; thereby they summoned Lue, and Liang sent him off with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 明帝詔光祿大夫刁雙境首勞問，除略侍中、義陽王。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming ordered Director of the Imperial Household Diao Shuang to meet and comfort him at the border; he made Lue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered Director of the Imperial Household Diao Shuang to meet and comfort him at the border; he made Lue attendant-in-ordinary and Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 還達石人驛亭，詔宗室親黨、內外百官先相識者，迎之近郊。

translations.literal: On reaching Shiren Post Pavilion, an edict ordered kinsmen of the imperial clan, inside and outside officials who knew him before, to welcome him in the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Shiren Post Pavilion, an edict ordered imperial kinsmen and inside and outside officials who knew him to welcome him in the near suburbs.

sentences.zh: 其司馬始賓除給事中，領直侯，栗法光本縣令，刁昌東平太守，刁雙西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: His marshal Shibin was made Gentleman-in-Attendance; Chief Gentleman of the Direct Attendance; Li Faguang was made magistrate of his native county; Diao Chang was made Administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang was made Governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His marshal Shibin was made gentleman-in-attendance and chief gentleman of the direct attendance; Li Faguang magistrate of his native county; Diao Chang administrator of Dongping; Diao Shuang governor of Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 略所經一食一宿處，無不沾賞。

translations.literal: Every place where Lue ate one meal or lodged one night was not without reward.
translations.idiomatic: Every place where Lue ate one meal or lodged one night was rewarded.

sentences.zh: 尋改封東平王，後為尚書令。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Prince of Dongping; later he was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Prince of Dongping; later he was made director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 靈太后甚寵任之，其見委信，殆與元徽相埒。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager greatly favored and trusted him; the trust shown him was nearly equal to Yuan Hui's.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager greatly favored and trusted him; the trust shown him nearly equaled Yuan Hui's.

sentences.zh: 于時天下多事，軍國萬端。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had many affairs; military and civil matters were myriad.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the realm had many affairs; military and civil matters were myriad.

sentences.zh: 略守常自保，無他裨益，唯具臣而已。

translations.literal: Lue kept to constancy and preserved himself; he had no other benefit—only a compliant minister.
translations.idiomatic: Lue kept to constancy and preserved himself; he had no other benefit—only a compliant minister.

sentences.zh: 爾硃滎，略之姑夫，略素所輕忽。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage; Lue had always looked down on him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong was Lue's uncle by marriage; Lue had always looked down on him lightly.

sentences.zh: 略又党于鄭儼、徐紇，榮兼銜之。

translations.literal: Lue again sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He; Rong harbored resentment on both counts.
translations.idiomatic: Lue again sided with Zheng Yan and Xu He; Rong harbored resentment on both counts.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛也，見害于河陰。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luoyang, Lue was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 加贈太保、司空公，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Duke of Works; his posthumous title was Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian and duke of works, posthumous title Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 英弟怡，位鄯善鎮將。

translations.literal: Ying's younger brother Yi held the office of General of the Shanshan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's younger brother Yi held the office of general of the Shanshan garrison.

sentences.zh: 在鎮貪暴，為有司所糾，逃免，卒。

translations.literal: In the garrison he was greedy and violent; the relevant offices impeached him; he fled and escaped punishment and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the garrison he was greedy and violent; the relevant offices impeached him; he fled, escaped punishment, and died.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，以爾硃榮婦兄，贈太尉、扶風王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's wife's elder brother, he was posthumously made Grand Duke of the Secretariat and Prince of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign, because he was Erzhu Rong's wife's elder brother, he was posthumously made grand duke of the Secretariat and Prince of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 子肅，封魯郡王。

translations.literal: His son Su was enfeoffed Prince of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su was enfeoffed Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 肅弟曄，字華興，小字盆子。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Ye, courtesy name Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Ye, courtesy name Huaxing, childhood name Penzi.

sentences.zh: 性輕躁，有膂力。

translations.literal: By nature he was frivolous and restless and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frivolous and restless and had physical strength.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，封長廣王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Changgang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangdi's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Changgang.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮死，世隆等推曄為主，年號建明。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others set up Ye as ruler; the era name was Jianming.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Shilong and the others set up Ye as ruler; the era name was Jianming.

sentences.zh: 尋為世隆廢。

translations.literal: Presently he was deposed by Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Shilong deposed him.

sentences.zh: 節閔立，封為東海王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jiemin was established, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jiemin was established, he was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，被殺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was killed.

sentences.zh: 城陽王長壽，皇興二年封，位沃野鎮都大將，甚有威名。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and held the office of Grand General of the Woye Garrison; he had a very great reputation for martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Changshou was enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing and held grand general of the Woye garrison; he had a very great reputation for martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡康王。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子鸞襲。

translations.literal: His son Luan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan inherited.

sentences.zh: 鸞字宣明，身長八尺，腰帶十圍。

translations.literal: Luan, courtesy name Xuanming, was eight chi in height; his belt measured ten arm-spans around.
translations.idiomatic: Luan, courtesy name Xuanming, stood eight chi; his belt measured ten arm-spans around.

sentences.zh: 以武藝稱，頻為北都大將。

translations.literal: He was famed for martial arts and repeatedly served as Grand General of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was famed for martial arts and repeatedly served as grand general of the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，除使持節、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made Bearer of the Staff and Southern Campaign Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was made bearer of the staff and southern campaign grand general.

sentences.zh: 與安南將軍盧陽烏、李佐攻赭陽不克，敗退，降為定襄縣王。

translations.literal: With Grand General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu and Li Zuo he attacked Zhiyang but could not take it; defeated, they withdrew; he was reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand General Who Pacifies the South Lu Yangwu and Li Zuo he attacked Zhiyang but could not take it; defeated, they withdrew; he was reduced to Prince of Dingxiang County.

sentences.zh: 後以留守功，還復本封。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in holding the rear, he was restored to his original enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for merit in holding the rear, he was restored to his original enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，為定州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 鸞愛樂佛道，繕起佛寺，勸率百姓，大為土木之勞，公私費擾，頗為人患。

translations.literal: Luan loved and delighted in Buddha's Way; he repaired Buddhist temples, urged and led the common people, and greatly labored them with earth and timber; public and private were troubled and he was much a nuisance to men.
translations.idiomatic: Luan loved Buddha's Way; he repaired temples, urged and led the people, and greatly labored them with earth and timber; public and private were troubled and he was much a nuisance.

sentences.zh: 宣武聞之，詔奪祿一周。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu heard of it, an edict stripped his salary for one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu heard of it, an edict stripped his salary for one cycle.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡懷王。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Huai.

sentences.zh: 子徽，字顯順，粗涉文史，頗有吏才。

translations.literal: His son Hui, courtesy name Xianshun, had slight knowledge of literature and history and considerable talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, courtesy name Xianshun, had slight knowledge of literature and history and considerable talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，襲封，為河內太守。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he inherited the enfeoffment and was Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he inherited the enfeoffment and was administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 在郡清整，有時譽。

translations.literal: In the commandery he was clear and orderly and had a reputation in the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the commandery he was clear and orderly and had a reputation in the age.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，為并州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was governor of Bing.

sentences.zh: 先是，州界夏霜，安業者少，徽輒開倉振之，文武咸共諫止。

translations.literal: Earlier, within the province's borders summer frost had fallen; those secure in their livelihoods were few; Hui at once opened the granaries to relieve them; civil and military officials all together remonstrated and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, within the province summer frost had fallen; those secure in livelihood were few; Hui at once opened the granaries to relieve them; civil and military officials all remonstrated and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 徽曰：「昔汲長孺郡守耳，尚輒開倉，救人災弊。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Formerly Ji Changru, though only a commandery administrator, still opened the granary to save men from disaster and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Formerly Ji Changru, though only a commandery administrator, still opened the granary to save men from disaster.

sentences.zh: 況我皇家親近，受委大籓，豈可拘法而不救人困也？

translations.literal: How much more I, a close kin of the imperial house, entrusted with a great frontier—how can I cling to the law and not save men in distress?"
translations.idiomatic: How much more I, close kin of the house, entrusted with a great frontier—how can I cling to the law and not save men in distress?"

sentences.zh: 」先給後奏。

translations.literal: He gave out first and memorialized afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He gave out first and memorialized afterward.

sentences.zh: 明帝嘉之，加安北將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming praised him and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming praised him and added the title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 汾州山胡舊多劫掠，自徽為郡，群胡自相戒，勿得侵擾鄰州。

translations.literal: The mountain Hu of Fen Province had long plundered heavily; from the time Hui was in the province the Hu groups warned one another not to disturb neighboring provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Hu of Fen had long plundered heavily; from the time Hui governed the province the Hu groups warned one another not to disturb neighboring provinces.

sentences.zh: 汾、肆之人多來詣徽投訴，願得口判。

translations.literal: Men of Fen and Si came in great numbers to Hui to lodge complaints, wishing to obtain his oral judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Fen and Si came in great numbers to lodge complaints with Hui, wishing to obtain his oral judgment.

sentences.zh: 除秦州刺史，還都，吏人泣涕攀車，不能自已。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Qin Province; on returning to the capital, officials and people wept, clinging to his carriage, unable to stop themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Qin; on returning to the capital, officials and people wept, clinging to his carriage, unable to stop themselves.

sentences.zh: 徽車馬羸弊，皆京來舊物，見者莫不歎其清儉。

translations.literal: Hui's carriage and horses were worn and thin—all old things from the capital; those who saw them all sighed at his integrity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's carriage and horses were worn and thin—all old things from the capital; onlookers sighed at his integrity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 改授度支尚書，兼吏部尚書，尋為正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Revenue and Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was made regular director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of revenue and concurrent director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was made regular director.

sentences.zh: 徽以選舉法期在得人，限以停年，有乖舊體。

translations.literal: Hui held that the law of selection aimed at obtaining the right men; limiting by years of service departed from the old body.
translations.idiomatic: Hui held that the law of selection aimed at obtaining the right men; limiting by years of service departed from the old body.

sentences.zh: 但行之日久，難以頓革，以德同者盡年，勞等者進德，于時稱為中平。

translations.literal: But it had been practiced long and was hard to change all at once; those equal in virtue received full years, those equal in merit advanced in virtue—men of the time called this "middling fairness."
translations.idiomatic: But it had been practiced long and was hard to change at once; those equal in virtue received full years, those equal in merit advanced in virtue—men of the time called this middling fairness.

sentences.zh: 除侍中，餘官如故。

translations.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary; the rest of his offices remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary; the rest of his offices remained as before.

sentences.zh: 徽表乞守一官。

translations.literal: Hui memorialized asking to hold only one office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized asking to hold only one office.

sentences.zh: 天下士子莫不歎息，咸曰：「城陽離選，貧者復何所希！

translations.literal: Scholars throughout the realm none did not sigh; all said: "Chengyang leaves selection—what may the poor still hope for!"
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the realm sighed and said, "Chengyang leaves selection—what may the poor still hope for!"

sentences.zh: 」怨嗟之聲，俄然上徹。

translations.literal: The sound of complaint and lament soon reached the heights.
translations.idiomatic: The sound of complaint and lament soon reached the heights.

sentences.zh: 還令兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was ordered back to hold Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered back to hold concurrent director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后專制，朝綱頹褫，徽既居寵任，無所匡弼。

translations.literal: At the time the Empress Dowager held sole power; court discipline was in ruins; though Hui occupied a favored post, he offered no correction.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Empress Dowager held sole power; court discipline was in ruins; though Hui occupied a favored post, he offered no correction.

sentences.zh: 與鄭儼之徒，更相阿黨。

translations.literal: With Zheng Yan and his sort he mutually formed factions.
translations.idiomatic: With Zheng Yan and his sort he mutually formed factions.

sentences.zh: 外似柔謹，內多猜忌，睚眥之忿，必思報復，識者疾之。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed gentle and careful; inwardly he was full of suspicion; the smallest grudge he was sure to repay—those who understood detested him.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed gentle and careful; inwardly he was full of suspicion; the smallest grudge he was sure to repay—those who understood detested him.

sentences.zh: 又不能防閑其妻于氏，遂與廣陽王深奸通。

translations.literal: He also could not restrain his wife Lady Yu; she then had illicit relations with Prince of Guangyang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He also could not restrain his wife Lady Yu; she then had illicit relations with Prince of Guangyang Shen.

sentences.zh: 及深受任軍府，每有表啟，論徽罪過，雖涉誣毀，頗亦實焉。

translations.literal: When Shen received command of the military government, in every memorial he discussed Hui's faults; though it involved slander, much of it was also true.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen received command of the military government, in every memorial he discussed Hui's faults; though it involved slander, much was also true.

sentences.zh: 莊帝踐阼，拜司州牧。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, Hui was made Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi ascended the throne, Hui was made governor of Si.

sentences.zh: 尋除司徒，仍領牧。

translations.literal: Presently he was made Duke of the Secretariat, still holding the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he was made duke of the Secretariat, still holding the governorship.

sentences.zh: 元顥之入洛，徽從莊帝北巡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hui followed Emperor Zhuangdi on the northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Hui followed Emperor Zhuangdi on the northern tour.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還宮，以與謀之功，除侍中、大司馬、太尉公，加羽葆鼓吹，增邑通前二萬戶。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, for merit in the plot he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Marshal, and Grand Duke of the Secretariat, with plumed canopy and war drums, and his fief increased to twenty thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, for merit in the plot he was made attendant-in-ordinary, grand marshal, and grand duke of the Secretariat, with plumed canopy and war drums, fief increased to twenty thousand households in all.

sentences.zh: 徽表辭官封，前後屢上。

translations.literal: Hui memorialized declining office and enfeoffment; he did so repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Hui memorialized declining office and enfeoffment repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 徽為莊帝親待，內懼爾硃榮等，故有此辭。

translations.literal: Hui was personally favored by Emperor Zhuangdi; inwardly he feared Erzhu Rong and the others; therefore he had this declination.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was personally favored by Emperor Zhuangdi; inwardly he feared Erzhu Rong and the others; therefore he declined.

sentences.zh: 莊帝識其意，聽其辭封，不許讓官。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangdi understood his meaning; he permitted him to decline the enfeoffment but did not permit him to decline office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood his meaning; he permitted decline of enfeoffment but not of office.

sentences.zh: 徽後妻，莊帝舅女。

translations.literal: Hui's later wife was the emperor's maternal uncle's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's later wife was the emperor's maternal uncle's daughter.

sentences.zh: 侍中李彧，帝之姊婿。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's elder sister's husband.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yu was the emperor's elder sister's husband.

sentences.zh: 徽性佞媚，善自取容，挾內外之意，宗室親寵，莫與比焉。

translations.literal: Hui by nature was fawning and ingratiating, skilled at winning favor for himself; he relied on inside and outside connections—among the imperial clan none was more favored.
translations.idiomatic: Hui by nature was fawning and ingratiating, skilled at winning favor; he relied on inside and outside connections—among the imperial clan none was more favored.

sentences.zh: 遂與彧等勸帝圖榮。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Yu and the others he urged the emperor to plot against Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon with Yu and the others he urged the emperor to plot against Rong.

sentences.zh: 莊帝亦先有意。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangdi too had long had the intention.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi too had long had the intention.

sentences.zh: 榮死，世隆等屯據不解。

translations.literal: When Rong died, Shilong and the others held their troops and would not disband.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, Shilong and the others held their troops and would not disband.

sentences.zh: 除徽太保，仍大司馬、宗師、錄尚書事，總統內外。

translations.literal: Hui was made Grand Guardian, still Grand Marshal, Grand Preceptor, and Recording Director, presiding over inside and outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was made grand guardian, still grand marshal, grand preceptor, and recording director, presiding over inside and outside affairs.

sentences.zh: 徽本意謂榮死後枝葉散亡。

translations.literal: Hui's original expectation was that after Rong's death the branches would scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's original expectation was that after Rong's death the branches would scatter.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃宗族聚結謀難，徽算略無出，憂怖而已。

translations.literal: When the Erzhu clan gathered and plotted trouble, Hui's stratagems had no outcome; he was only fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When the Erzhu clan gathered and plotted trouble, Hui's stratagems had no outcome; he was only fearful.

sentences.zh: 性多嫉妒，不欲人居其前。

translations.literal: By nature he was very jealous and did not wish others to stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was very jealous and did not wish others to stand before him.

sentences.zh: 每入參謀議，獨與帝決。

translations.literal: Whenever he entered to discuss strategy he alone decided with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered to discuss strategy he alone decided with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有上軍國籌策者，並勸帝不納。

translations.literal: If court officials memorialized military and state plans, he all urged the emperor not to accept.
translations.idiomatic: If court officials memorialized military and state plans, he urged the emperor not to accept.

sentences.zh: 乃云：「小賊何慮不除？

translations.literal: He would say: "What worry is there that small bandits cannot be eliminated?"
translations.idiomatic: He would say, "What worry is there that small bandits cannot be eliminated?"

sentences.zh: 」又惜財用，于時有所賞錫，咸出薄少，或多而中減，與而復追。

translations.literal: He also was stingy with wealth; at the time whenever there were rewards and gifts they were all thin and few, or if many they were cut down midway, given and then pursued for return.
translations.idiomatic: He was also stingy with wealth; whenever there were rewards they were thin and few, or if many they were cut down midway, given and then pursued for return.

sentences.zh: 莊帝雅自約狹，尤亦徽所贊成。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangdi by nature was himself narrow and sparing; Hui especially approved and shaped this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi by nature was narrow and sparing; Hui especially approved and shaped this.

sentences.zh: 太府少卿李苗，徽司徒時司馬也，徽待之頗厚。

translations.literal: Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury Li Miao, when Hui was Duke of the Secretariat had been his marshal; Hui treated him quite generously.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Director of the Imperial Treasury Li Miao, when Hui was duke of the Secretariat, had been his marshal; Hui treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 苗每致忠言，徽多不採納。

translations.literal: Miao often offered loyal words; Hui mostly did not adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: Miao often offered loyal words; Hui mostly did not adopt them.

sentences.zh: 苗謂人曰：「城陽本自蜂目，而豺聲復將露也。

translations.literal: Miao told others: "Chengyang by nature has the eyes of a wasp, and now the voice of a jackal will also show."
translations.idiomatic: Miao told others, "Chengyang by nature has the eyes of a wasp, and now the voice of a jackal will also show."

sentences.zh: 」及爾硃兆之入，禁衛奔散，莊帝步出雲龍門，徽乘馬奔度，帝頻呼之，徽不顧而去。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered, the palace guards scattered in flight; Emperor Zhuangdi walked out the Cloud Dragon Gate; Hui mounted his horse and fled across; the emperor repeatedly called him; Hui did not look back and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered, palace guards scattered; Emperor Zhuangdi walked out the Cloud Dragon Gate; Hui mounted and fled across; the emperor repeatedly called; Hui did not look back.

sentences.zh: 遂走山南，至故吏寇彌宅。

translations.literal: He then fled to the south of the mountains, to the house of his former subordinate Kou Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to the south of the mountains, to the house of his former subordinate Kou Mi.

sentences.zh: 彌外雖容納，內不自安，乃怖徽云：「官捕將至。

translations.literal: Mi outwardly received him but inwardly was not at ease; he then frightened Hui, saying: "Official arrest is about to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Mi outwardly received him but inwardly was uneasy; he frightened Hui, saying, "Official arrest is about to arrive."
