sentences.zh: 」令其避他所，使人于路邀害，送屍於爾硃兆。

translations.literal: He ordered him to avoid another place; he had men lie in wait on the road and kill him, then sent the corpse to Erzhu Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him to another place; he had men lie in wait on the road and kill him, then sent the corpse to Erzhu Zhao.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，贈使持節、侍中、太師、錄尚書事、司州牧，諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Preceptor, Recording Director, and Governor of Si Province; his posthumous title was Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made bearer of the staff, attendant-in-ordinary, grand preceptor, recording director, and governor of Si, posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 子延襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent the rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, by precedent the rank was reduced.

sentences.zh: 章武王太洛，皇興二年薨，追贈征北大將軍、章武郡王，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in the second year of Huangxing; posthumously made Northern Campaign Grand General and Prince of Zhangwu Commandery; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhangwu Tailuo died in the second year of Huangxing; posthumously made northern campaign grand general and Prince of Zhangwu, posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，以南安惠王第二子彬為後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen, the second son of Prince of Nan'an Hui, Bin, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen, the second son of Prince of Nan'an Hui, Bin, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 彬字豹兒，勇健有將用。

translations.literal: Bin, courtesy name Bao'er, was brave and strong and had the talent of a general.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, courtesy name Bao'er, was brave and strong and had the talent of a general.

sentences.zh: 為夏州刺史，以貪婪削封。

translations.literal: He was Governor of Xia Province; for greed his enfeoffment was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was governor of Xia; for greed his enfeoffment was stripped.

sentences.zh: 後除汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Fen Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Fen.

sentences.zh: 胡六百餘人保險謀反。

translations.literal: More than six hundred Hu held difficult terrain and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: More than six hundred Hu held difficult terrain and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 彬請兵二萬，帝大怒曰：「必須大眾者，則先斬刺史，然後發兵！

translations.literal: Bin asked for twenty thousand troops; the emperor was greatly angered and said: "If a great host is truly needed, first behead the governor, then raise the army!"
translations.idiomatic: Bin asked for twenty thousand troops; the emperor was greatly angered and said, "If a great host is truly needed, first behead the governor, then raise the army!"

sentences.zh: 」彬奉詔大懼，身先將士，討胡平之。

translations.literal: Bin received the edict in great fear; he himself led the soldiers first and pacified the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Bin received the edict in great fear; he himself led the soldiers first and pacified the Hu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously made regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子融，字永興，儀貌壯麗，性通率有豪氣。

translations.literal: His son Rong, courtesy name Yongxing, had a magnificent appearance and by nature was open and direct with heroic spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong, courtesy name Yongxing, had a magnificent appearance and by nature was open and direct with heroic spirit.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，復先爵，累遷河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu his former title was restored; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu his former title was restored; he rose to governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 融性尤貪欲，恣情聚斂，為中尉糾彈，削除官爵。

translations.literal: Rong was especially greedy; he indulged in gathering wealth and was impeached by the chief commandant; his office and rank were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was especially greedy; he indulged in gathering wealth and was impeached by the chief commandant; office and rank were stripped.

sentences.zh: 汾、夏山胡叛逆，連結正平、平陽。

translations.literal: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Hu of Fen and Xia rebelled, linking Zhengping and Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 詔復融前封，征東將軍、持節、都督以討之。

translations.literal: An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment; he was made Eastern Campaign General, Bearer of the Staff, and Commander-in-Chief to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Rong's former enfeoffment; he was made eastern campaign general, bearer of the staff, and commander-in-chief to attack them.

sentences.zh: 融寡于經略，為胡所敗。

translations.literal: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was weak in strategy and was defeated by the Hu.

sentences.zh: 後賊帥鮮于修禮寇暴瀛、定二州，長孫承業等討之失利。

translations.literal: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli raided Ying and Ding provinces; Zhangsun Chengye and others campaigned against him and failed.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandit chief Xianyu Xiuli raided Ying and Ding; Zhangsun Chengye and others campaigned against him and failed.

sentences.zh: 除融車騎將軍，為前驅左軍都督，與廣陽王深等共討修禮。

translations.literal: Rong was made General of the Imperial Chariots and vanguard left-army commander-in-chief; with Prince of Guangyang Shen and others he jointly attacked Xiuli.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was made general of the imperial chariots and vanguard left-army commander-in-chief; with Prince of Guangyang Shen and others he jointly attacked Xiuli.

sentences.zh: 師度交津，葛榮殺修禮而自立，轉營至白牛邏，輕騎擊融，於陣見殺。

translations.literal: The army crossed the Jiao Ford; Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up; he shifted camp to Bainiu Ford; light cavalry struck Rong and killed him in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed the Jiao Ford; Ge Rong killed Xiuli and set himself up; he shifted camp to Bainiu Ford; light cavalry struck Rong and killed him in the formation.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made duke of works.

sentences.zh: 尋以融死王事，進贈司徒公，加前後部鼓吹，諡莊武。

translations.literal: Presently because Rong died in the prince's service, he was advanced posthumously to Duke of the Secretariat, with front and rear war drums added; his posthumous title was Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Presently because Rong died in the prince's service, he was advanced posthumously to duke of the Secretariat with front and rear war drums added, posthumous title Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 子景哲襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingzhe inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingzhe inherited.

sentences.zh: 景哲弟朗，即廢帝也。

translations.literal: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang was the deposed emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhe's younger brother Lang was the deposed emperor.

sentences.zh: 樂陵王胡兒，和平四年薨，追封樂陵王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Prince of Leling Hu'er died in the fourth year of Heping; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Leling; his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Leling Hu'er died in the fourth year of Heping; posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Leling, posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son.

sentences.zh: 獻文詔胡兒兄汝陰王天賜之第二子永全後之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen ordered the second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince of Ruyin Tiansi, Yongquan, to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen ordered the second son of Hu'er's elder brother Prince of Ruyin Tiansi, Yongquan, to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 襲封後，改名思譽。

translations.literal: After inheriting the enfeoffment he changed his name to Siyu.
translations.idiomatic: After inheriting the enfeoffment he changed his name to Siyu.

sentences.zh: 孝文時，為鎮北大將軍。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was Grand General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 穆泰陰謀不軌，思譽知而不告，削封為庶人。

translations.literal: Mu Tai secretly plotted disloyalty; Siyu knew and did not report it; his enfeoffment was stripped and he was made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Tai secretly plotted disloyalty; Siyu knew and did not report it; his enfeoffment was stripped and he was made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 太和末，復王封。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe his princely enfeoffment was restored.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡密王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Mi.

sentences.zh: 子景略襲，位豳州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Jinglüe succeeded and held the post of governor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinglüe succeeded and served as governor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡惠王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 安定王休，皇興二年封。

translations.literal: Prince of Anding Xiu, enfeoffed in the second year of Huangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anding Xiu was enfeoffed in Huangxing 2.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and keen.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and quick.

sentences.zh: 為外都大官，斷獄有稱。

translations.literal: As Grand Judge of the Outer Capital he was famed for deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Judge of the Outer Capital he won fame for judging cases.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，領大司馬。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, he headed the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: When the court campaigned south, he headed the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 孝文親行諸軍，遇休以三盜人徇六軍，將斬之，有詔赦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen personally reviewed the armies; he met Xiu taking three thieves to parade before the six armies and about to behead them, but an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen reviewed the armies in person and found Xiu parading three thieves before the six armies to behead them; an edict pardoned the men.

sentences.zh: 休執曰：「不斬何以息盜？

translations.literal: Xiu held fast and said: "If they are not beheaded, how can theft be stilled?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiu held fast and said, "If they are not beheaded, how will theft be stilled?"

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「王者之體，亦時有非常之澤，雖違軍法，可特原之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The kingly body also has times of extraordinary grace; though this violates military law, they may be specially spared."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, "A king may show extraordinary grace; though this breaks military law, spare them."

sentences.zh: 」休乃奉詔。

translations.literal: Xiu then obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu then obeyed the edict.

sentences.zh: 帝謂司徒馮誕曰：「大司馬嚴而執法，諸軍不可不慎。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Minister of Education Feng Dan: "The Grand Marshal is stern and holds to the law—the armies must be careful."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Minister of Education Feng Dan, "The Grand Marshal is stern in law—the armies must take care."

sentences.zh: 」於是六軍肅然。

translations.literal: Thereupon the six armies were all in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the six armies stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 定都洛邑，休從駕幸鄴，命休率從駕文武迎家于平城，帝親餞休于漳水之北。

translations.literal: When the capital was fixed at Luoyang, Xiu followed the carriage to Ye; he was ordered to lead the civil and military who followed the carriage to bring their families from Pingcheng; the emperor personally saw Xiu off north of the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, Xiu followed the court to Ye, led the following officials to fetch their families from Pingcheng, and was seen off by the emperor north of the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 十八年，休寢疾，帝幸其第，流涕問疾，中使醫藥相望于路。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Xiu took to his bed ill; the emperor visited his residence, weeping as he inquired after him; palace envoys with medicine and physicians filled the road one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Xiu fell ill; the emperor visited his house in tears, and envoys with physicians crowded the road.

sentences.zh: 及薨至殯，車駕三臨。

translations.literal: From death until the encoffining the imperial carriage visited three times.
translations.idiomatic: From his death until the encoffining the emperor visited three times.

sentences.zh: 帝至其門，改服錫衰，素弁加絰。

translations.literal: The emperor came to his gate, changed into coarse hemp, plain cap with mourning headband.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to his gate, changed into coarse hemp mourning dress, plain cap with headband.

sentences.zh: 皇太子百官皆從行吊禮。

translations.literal: The crown prince and all officials followed in performing mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince and all officials followed in the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靖王。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 詔贈假黃鉞，加羽葆鼓吹，悉准三老尉元之儀。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted the golden axe of authority, added feathered canopy and martial pipes, all matching the rites of the Elder of State Wei Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him posthumously the golden axe, feathered canopy, and martial pipes, all matching Elder of State Wei Yuan.

sentences.zh: 帝親送出郭，慟哭而返。

translations.literal: The emperor personally escorted him beyond the outer wall, weeping as he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor escorted him beyond the wall and returned weeping.

sentences.zh: 諸王恩禮莫比。

translations.literal: No prince received such favor in rites.
translations.idiomatic: No other prince was honored with such rites.

sentences.zh: 宣武世，配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was given sacrifice in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he received sacrifice in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子超，字化生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chao, courtesy name Huasheng, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao, courtesy Huasheng, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 時以胡國珍封安定公，改封北平王，後復本封。

translations.literal: At the time Hu Guozhen was enfeoffed Duke of Anding; he was changed to Prince of Beiping, later restored to his original enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu Guozhen held Duke of Anding; Chao was shifted to Prince of Beiping, then restored to Anding.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮入洛，避難見害。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he was killed while seeking refuge.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he was killed while seeking refuge.

sentences.zh: 景山字寶嶽，少有器局，幹略過人。

translations.literal: Jingshan, courtesy name Baoyue, in youth had capacity and vision, and ability surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan, courtesy Baoyue, had capacity and vision in youth and ability beyond most men.

sentences.zh: 周景帝時，以軍功累遷開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Jing of Zhou he was repeatedly promoted for military merit to Commissioner with the Golden Seal and equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing of Zhou he rose by military merit to Commissioner with the Golden Seal, equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 從武帝平齊，以功拜大將軍、平原郡公、亳州總管。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, for merit he was made Grand General, Duke of Pingyuan commandery, and Commander of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Wu in pacifying Qi, he was made Grand General, Duke of Pingyuan, and Commander of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 法令明肅，賊盜屏跡，部內大清。

translations.literal: His laws were clear and stern, bandits vanished from his tracks, and within his jurisdiction all was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: His laws were clear and stern, bandits vanished, and his district grew quiet.

sentences.zh: 徵為候正。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Director of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be Director of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，從上柱國韋孝寬經略淮南。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he followed the Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he followed Senior Pillar of State Wei Xiaokuan in planning for Huainan.

sentences.zh: 鄖州總管宇文亮反，以輕兵襲孝寬。

translations.literal: Commander of Yunzhou Yuwen Liang rebelled and with light troops struck Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: Commander of Yunzhou Yuwen Liang rebelled and struck Xiaokuan with light troops.

sentences.zh: 寬為亮所薄，景山擊破之。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan was pressed by Liang; Jingshan struck and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan was hard pressed; Jingshan struck and broke Liang.

sentences.zh: 以功拜亳州總管。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Commander of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was again made Commander of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，尉遲迥作亂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yu Chi Jiong rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Yu Chi Jiong rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 榮州刺史宇文胄與迥通謀，陰以書諷景山。

translations.literal: Governor of Rongzhou Yuwen Zhou conspired with Jiong and secretly sent a letter to urge Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Rongzhou Yuwen Zhou conspired with Jiong and secretly urged Jingshan by letter.

sentences.zh: 景山執使，封書詣相府，進位上大將軍。

translations.literal: Jingshan seized the envoy, sealed the letter, and sent it to the chief minister's office; he was advanced to Grand General Supreme.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan seized the envoy, sealed the letter, and sent it to the chief minister's office, and was advanced to Grand General Supreme.

sentences.zh: 以軍功，遷安州總管，進柱國。

translations.literal: For military merit he was transferred to Commander of Anzhou and advanced to Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: For military merit he was made Commander of Anzhou and advanced to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was made Senior Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the throne, he was made Senior Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 明年，大舉伐陳，以景山為行軍元帥，出漢口。

translations.literal: The next year, in a great campaign against Chen, Jingshan was made campaign commander-in-chief and marched out of Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the great campaign against Chen, Jingshan was commander-in-chief and marched from Hankou.

sentences.zh: 將濟江，會陳宣帝殂，有詔班師。

translations.literal: About to cross the Yangzi, it happened that Emperor Xuan of Chen died; an edict ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: About to cross the Yangzi, he learned that Emperor Xuan of Chen had died; an edict ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 景山大著威名，甚為敵人所憚。

translations.literal: Jingshan's great fame made the enemy deeply fear him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshan's fame was so great that enemies deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 後數載，坐事免。

translations.literal: Several years later, for an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 卒于家，贈梁州總管，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: He died at home; posthumously made Commander of Liangzhou, posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home and was posthumously made Commander of Liangzhou, posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子成壽嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chengshou succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengshou succeeded.

sentences.zh: 成壽便弓馬，為秦王庫直。

translations.literal: Chengshou was skilled in bow and horse and served as armory attendant to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Chengshou was skilled with bow and horse and served as armory attendant to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為西平郡通守。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was Commandant of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he was Commandant of Xiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 燮弟願平，清狂無行。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and unrestrained in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Yuanping was wild and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為給事中，悖惡日甚，殺人劫盜，公私咸患。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Supervising Attendant; his depravity grew daily—murder, robbery, public and private all suffered.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Supervising Attendant; his depravity grew daily in murder and robbery until all suffered.

sentences.zh: 帝以戚近，不忍致之法；

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was close kin, could not bear to bring him under the law;
translations.idiomatic: Because he was close kin, the emperor could not bear to punish him by law;

sentences.zh: 免官，禁之別館。

translations.literal: he was removed from office and confined in a separate lodge.
translations.idiomatic: he was removed from office and confined in a separate lodge.

sentences.zh: 館名悉思堂，冀其克念。

translations.literal: The lodge was named Hall of Complete Reflection, in hope he would restrain his thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: The lodge was named Hall of Complete Reflection, in hope he would restrain his thoughts.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，乃得出。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, he was then able to come out.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, he was allowed out.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，以其不悛，還於別館，依前禁錮。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because he would not reform, he was returned to the separate lodge and confined as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, because he would not reform, he was returned to the lodge and confined as before.

sentences.zh: 久之，離禁還家，付宗師嚴加誨獎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was released to his home and handed to the Imperial Clan Director for strict admonition and guidance.
translations.idiomatic: After long confinement he was released home and handed to the Imperial Clan Director for strict guidance.

sentences.zh: 後拜通直散騎常侍、前將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry on the Direct Path and Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry on the Direct Path and Forward General.

sentences.zh: 坐裸其妻王氏于其男女前，又強姦妻妹于妻母之側，御史中尉侯剛案以不道，處絞刑。

translations.literal: For stripping his wife Lady Wang naked before their sons and daughters, and also forcing his wife's younger sister before her mother, Chief Commandant Hou Gang judged it unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: For stripping his wife Lady Wang before their children and raping her sister before her mother, Chief Commandant Hou Gang judged unnatural conduct and sentenced him to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 會赦免，黜為員外常侍。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and was spared; demoted to Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him; he was demoted to Regular Attendant Outside the Sequence.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陽平諸子，頤乃忠壯。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Among the sons of Yangping, Yi alone was loyal and stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Among the sons of Yangping, Yi alone was loyal and stalwart.

sentences.zh: 京兆之胤，忄妻實有聲。

translations.literal: Of the Jingzhao succession, 忄妻 truly had a name.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Jingzhao line, Xun truly had a name.

sentences.zh: 匡之謇直，有足稱矣！

translations.literal: Kuang's blunt uprightness is well worth praise!
translations.idiomatic: Kuang's blunt uprightness is well worth praise!

sentences.zh: 當獻文將禪，可謂國之大節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianwen was about to abdicate, it may be called the great integrity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianwen was about to abdicate, it was the great test of the state's integrity.

sentences.zh: 康王毅然廷諍，德音孔昭，一言興邦，斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly at court; his virtuous words shone clear—one word raised the state; is this not what is meant?
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang remonstrated firmly in court; his virtuous words shone—one sentence raised the state; is this not the thing?

sentences.zh: 文宣貞固俊遠，郁為宗傑，身用累朝。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was upright, firm, lofty, and far-seeing, luxuriant as a clan hero, serving many reigns in person.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan was upright, firm, lofty, and far-seeing, a luxuriant hero of the clan who served many reigns in person.

sentences.zh: 寧濟夷險，社稷是任，其梁棟之望乎！

translations.literal: Calm in ease and danger alike, he bore the altars of state—is this not the hope of a beam and pillar?
translations.idiomatic: Calm in ease and danger alike, he bore the altars of state—the very hope of beam and pillar.

sentences.zh: 順蹇諤俶儻，有汲黯之風，不用於時，橫招非命，惜矣！

translations.literal: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the air of Ji An; unused in his time, he met violent death by chance—a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Shun was blunt in remonstrance and free in spirit, with the air of Ji An; unused in his time, he met violent death by chance—a pity!

sentences.zh: 嵩有行陣之氣，俊乃裂冠之徒。

translations.literal: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was a man who tore the cap.
translations.idiomatic: Song had the spirit of the battle line; Jun was a man who tore the cap.

sentences.zh: 南安原始要終，善不掩惡。

translations.literal: Nan'an traced beginning and end; good did not cover evil.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'an traced beginning and end; good did not cover evil.

sentences.zh: 英將帥之用，著聲于時。

translations.literal: Ying's use as commander and general made a name in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's use as commander made a name in his time.

sentences.zh: 熙、略兄弟，早播人譽，或才疏志大，或器狹任廣。

translations.literal: The brothers Xi and Lüe early spread men's praise; one was talented but his aim too large, one narrow in capacity yet given wide charge.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Xi and Lüe won early praise; one had talent but aims too large, one narrow in capacity yet given wide charge.

sentences.zh: 咸不能就其功名，俱至非命，惜也！

translations.literal: None could finish their fame and merit; all met untimely death—a pity!
translations.idiomatic: None could finish their fame; all met untimely death—a pity!

sentences.zh: 康王不永，鸞起家聲。

translations.literal: Prince Kang was not long-lived; Luan raised the family's name.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang was not long-lived; Luan raised the family's name.

sentences.zh: 徽飾智矯情，外諂內忌，永安之禍，誰任其責？

translations.literal: Hui adorned his wit and bent his feelings, fawning outside while jealous within—the disaster of Yong'an, who bore the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Hui adorned his wit and bent his feelings, fawning outside while jealous within—the disaster of Yong'an: who bore the blame?

sentences.zh: 宛其死也，固其宜哉！

translations.literal: When he died, it was surely fitting!
translations.idiomatic: When he died, it was surely fitting!

sentences.zh: 章武、樂陵，蓋不足數。

translations.literal: Zhangwu and Leling scarcely count.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangwu and Leling scarcely count.

sentences.zh: 靖王聽斷威重，見稱於太和，美矣！

translations.literal: Prince Jing was decisive in judgment, stern in authority, praised in the Taihe era—beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing judged decisively and bore stern authority, praised in the Taihe era—beautiful!
